note: The failures scripts/verify/probe-smoke-test.py finds on a CLEAN TREE, so that a
NEW failure - one your changes caused - is not buried under eighteen old ones.
Every check still runs on every file and every failure is still printed. This
file only decides which of them you have to think about.
ADD A ROW only after you have proved the failure is older than your work:
git log -1 --format=%cd -- <path>   and read the probe.
Give it a reason, a bucket, today's date, and a clears_when that says what has
to become true for the row to be deleted. DELETE A ROW the moment the probe
passes - the checker prints PASSES NOW for a row that no longer fails, because
a baseline nobody prunes is where failures go to be forgotten.
BUCKETS are PROMPTS.md's two: environment (the box has not run setup) and
defect (the probe cannot start for its own reasons). All eighteen rows here are
defect, which is not what the messages look like: ten of them end in the path
of a missing llama-server, which reads as environment. It is not. Each of those
ten has NO ARGUMENT PARSER, so `--help` is not answered, it is RUN - and the
missing binary is only where the run stops first. DERIVED, not measured here:
with llama.cpp built those ten do not clear, they stop later - at the dry-run
GPU fence, since probe-smoke-test.py sets MEASURED_INFERENCE_DRY_RUN=1.
'A help request must never start work' is the standing rule; see the comment in
scripts/quant-ladder/three-file-12gb-fit.py, which overwrote its own result file
under a smoke test before it grew a --help test.
